title: Is an Energy Surplus Required to Maximize Skeletal Muscle Hypertrophy Associated With Resistance Training? (Slater et al. 2019)
content: Slater GJ et al., Frontiers in Nutrition 2019 — Reviews evidence that meaningful muscle hypertrophy from resistance training can occur without a caloric surplus, and even during an energy deficit, particularly in novice trainees, individuals with higher starting body-fat levels, or those returning to training after a layoff (i.e. 'body recomposition' candidates). A surplus is not a strict physiological requirement for hypertrophy for every trainee.

title: Is an Energy Surplus Required to Maximize Skeletal Muscle Hypertrophy Associated With Resistance Training? (Slater et al. 2019)
content: Slater et al. 2019 — Product implication: an AI coach should not assume every muscle-gain goal requires a calorie surplus by default — for beginners or higher-body-fat individuals, a maintenance or even a modest deficit can support both fat loss and some muscle gain simultaneously. A surplus becomes more clearly necessary for advanced/lean trainees closer to their genetic ceiling.
